clue.text: Abandon California and North Carolina to the Spanish

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
NC is the postal abbreviation for North Carolina
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to give up two American states and hand them over to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To call off or scrap a plan is to drop it entirely, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Boy and girl give gifts to the poor

parts.note: Al is a boy's name, short for Alan or Albert
Ms is the title used before a woman's name

explanation.surface: A young couple hand out presents to people in need.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity given as money or food to needy people has long been called by this old church word.

clue.text: Barbie can frolic in the sea

indicators.note: to frolic is to romp about playfully, so the letters skip out of their order

parts.note: the doll's name and the next word, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A Barbie doll is pictured playing about in the ocean on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the body of water between Central America and the West Indies, an arm of the Atlantic.

clue.text: Desire religious eduction in order to shine

parts.note: lust is strong desire
RE is the school subject Religious Education; the clue's 'eduction' is a typo for education

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a bit of Sunday school will make them sparkle.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Religious Education) is a lesson on the British school timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloss or sheen on a polished surface is its glow, so the noun matches shine in that sense.

clue.text: Mighty soldier is acting strangely

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: doing something strangely means doing it in an odd, disordered way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A powerful soldier is behaving oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of enormous size or strength, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Scarlett's story is carried away on the breeze

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the novel and film whose heroine is Scarlett O'Hara
second meaning: literally blown off by moving air

explanation.walkthrough: The title of Margaret Mitchell's novel read literally describes something blown off by air.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell's Civil War novel follows Scarlett O'Hara, and its title literally describes something blown off.

clue.text: Tears get spilled, but it's for the best

indicators.note: spilled things are scattered and disordered, so the letters fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: the two words letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone cries but consoles themselves that it all turned out well.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are superlatives of good or great, naming whatever is top of its class.

clue.text: Speed to New York in spirit

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
speed is measured in mph, miles per hour

explanation.surface: Someone races to New York full of enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed to New York' means the speed unit is attached to New York, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a nymph is a minor female nature spirit living in woods, rivers or seas.

clue.text: Barges in, making priest turn round

indicators.note: turning things round mixes up their order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone bursts into a room and makes the priest spin about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' does double duty in the surface, but its letters are part of the fodder while 'turn round' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in on a conversation is to break into it rudely, which is what someone who cuts in does.

clue.text: Cage mischief-maker up? No, sir!

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little creature

indicators.note: going up reads the words in the opposite direction, from end to start

parts.note: the words taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a suggestion that a troublemaker be locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock someone in a cell or pen is to jail them, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Hatred? The heartless enemy will embrace it

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms round, so one piece goes around the other
without a heart means the central letter is removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written, then its middle letter dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A callous foe is shown welcoming hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep mutual hostility between people or nations is a form of strong ill will.

clue.text: Does girl's audience consist of twitchers?

parts.note: bird is British slang for a young woman
an audience is the people watching

explanation.surface: A question about whether a young woman's fans are nervous fidgeters.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is informal British slang for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitcher is a British nickname for an obsessive bird-spotter who rushes to see rare species.

clue.text: Is this fat monk watching you?

definitions.text: Is this fat monk watching you?

parts.note: fat means large
a monk is addressed as Brother

explanation.surface: Someone nervously asks whether a portly monk is keeping an eye on them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue echoes the Orwell slogan from Nineteen Eighty-Four, 'Big Brother is watching you'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's novel the all-seeing leader appears on posters with the warning that he is always observing citizens.

clue.text: It's a thousand to one that Ted loses 500 on "Bird of Prey"

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: K stands for a thousand
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Betting odds of a thousand to one, with Ted losing a big stake on a horse called Bird of Prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The red kite is a raptor of the hawk family, so it is an example of a bird of prey.

clue.text: When in race, take new fuel to be refined

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Instructions to a racing driver to top up with fresh petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with refined manners or taste shows good judgment and elegance, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Secretly listen to most of the leaves fall

indicators.note: most of a word means it is not all there, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its first letter
to fall is to drop

explanation.surface: An autumn scene of leaves coming down from the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'most of' drops the first letter rather than the usual last one.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to overhear a private conversation on purpose without the speakers knowing.

clue.text: Germs? A scholar caught one in time!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar
ct is a cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
an era is a period of time
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a student has caught a single bug just before the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' gives CT here, the scorecard abbreviation, rather than the usual single C.
explanation.definitionFit: Germ is the everyday word for a microbe that causes disease, and these microbes are the commonest kind.

clue.text: One cake and mashed tea is plenty to start

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: mashing pulps things into a jumble, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of tea

explanation.surface: A cake and a cup of tea make a filling snack before the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' sits after the definition but selects from tea.
explanation.definitionFit: When there is plenty of something it exists in large, more than sufficient quantity.

clue.text: Checks on old soldiers

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a welfare visit to retired servicemen; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet is to examine thoroughly, and vets is informal shorthand for veterans of the armed forces.

clue.text: Stew made with spicy grass

parts.note: spicy food is hot
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A recipe for a stew flavoured with a pungent herb.
explanation.walkthrough: A hotpot is a British stew of meat topped with sliced potatoes, associated with Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire hotpot is a slow-cooked casserole of lamb and potatoes, so it is a kind of stew.

clue.text: Bloomers displayed in order to procure chaps' love on back street

parts.note: for can mean in order to, as in 'go for a walk'
to procure is to get
chaps are men
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from end to start

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Underwear is put on show in the hope of winning men's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like old-fashioned knickers, but here it means flowers, things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Forget-me-nots are small blue flowers, so they are bloomers in the punning sense of things that bloom.

clue.text: Assumed that the end of the war in Europe was part of a trap

indicators.note: being part of something puts it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

parts.words: the end of the war in Europe
parts.note: VE stands for Victory in Europe, the end of the Second World War there

explanation.surface: Someone supposes that the 1945 victory in Europe was a set-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Given and assumed both mean taken for granted, as in 'given that' meaning 'assuming that'.

clue.text: Cure the alopecia internally

indicators.note: internally points inside the words that follow, where the letters sit

parts.note: found inside these words across the gap

explanation.surface: A doctor's goal of treating baldness from within.
explanation.walkthrough: Alopecia is the medical name for hair loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure an illness is to make the patient well again, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Pam, the tennis player, loses right to smash

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter goes from the name

parts.note: Pam Shriver was an American tennis champion of the 1980s
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A tennis player loses her serve to an opponent's powerful smash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smash' looks like a tennis shot, but it is the definition, as in breaking to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver something is an old word for shattering it into fragments, as in 'shiver my timbers'.

clue.text: I'm to the left of the editor who was brought in

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
port is the left side of a ship
ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone describes their position relative to a newly hired editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are imported have been bought from abroad and carried into the country.

clue.text: Toper intoxicated, lying by a road

parts.note: intoxicated means drunk
taken as written
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker sprawled out by the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is an old word for a habitual heavy drinker, someone constantly under the influence.

clue.text: In future, stop please, or you'll fall

indicators.note: in points inside the words that follow, where the letters sit

parts.note: found inside these words, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A warning to slow down before you take a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple is to tip over and come crashing down, a close synonym of fall.
